archetype.name: Pocket Passer (under siege)
archetype.definition: A big-armed, 6-foot-6 thrower who wins from the pocket and has produced positive EPA every year of his career. He is now stuck behind the league's leakiest protection in a run-first offense that leaves him passing on long downs.

report.headline: A proven passer drowning in sacks, long downs and late-game collapses
report.take:
Herbert's career says he is a good starting quarterback. Across six seasons his EPA per play never dipped below 0.065, and he spent most of those years in the top half of the league in yards and touchdowns. This year he sits 42nd of 45 in EPA per dropback at -0.223, the Chargers are 0-6, and his pace has him throwing 23 interceptions and taking 60 sacks. That isn't a gradual decline. It's a cliff, and a cliff needs a cause.

The biggest cause is the environment. Opponents hit his quarterbacks more often than any other offense's (offensive hit rate 32nd), and he is sacked on 10.4% of dropbacks. Harbaugh's offense passes far less than situation predicts, 11.4 points under expected and the lowest in the league, but the run game is 30th in EPA. So the passes come in bad spots: third downs average 8.7 yards to go and get converted 32.3% of the time. Some of it is him, though. His pressure-to-sack rate has climbed for years, from 17.1% as a rookie to 33.3% in 2024, and it is 36.2% now. Holding the ball has become part of who he is. His accuracy has also slipped badly: CPOE is -5.66 against +1.6 last year, and his bad-throw rate is up 3.4 points.

The totals hide how concentrated the damage is. Close fourth-quarter snaps, only 28 plays, account for -32.3 EPA, with 9 sacks and 2 picks, out of -52.5 on all his dropbacks. Outside those moments he has been poor, not catastrophic. The depth split is also counterintuitive. Throws of 10+ air yards are roughly break-even at -0.005 per play even though they hold 7 of his 8 interceptions. The real drain is the short game at -0.132 per play, including screens and checkdowns at -0.174. His tight end has been a sinkhole: Oronde Gadsden II has produced -11 EPA on 21 targets. Ladd McConkey has been the opposite at +0.66 per target.

The recent slide (-0.308 per dropback over the last three games) came against Seattle, Denver and Kansas City, three defenses now ranked in the top five. That explains some of it but excuses little, because he also lost all three early games as a favorite or near-even against bottom-ten defenses. The concentrated late-game disaster and an accuracy drop this far from his norm both point to some bounce back toward his career baseline. A protection unit this bad and his own sack habit cap how far that bounce goes.

strengths.title: Downfield throws still break even
strengths.body: His 10+ air-yard attempts are essentially neutral per play, and intermediate throws are slightly positive with a 48.9% success rate. The arm that produced 5,000-yard seasons still creates value when he gets time to drive the ball. The interceptions are the tax on it, and his career interception rates suggest they are running hot.

strengths.title: Legs keep drives alive
strengths.body: He ranks 6th among qualifiers in rushing yards, and his output has risen lately to 40 a game over the last three. That fits a player who ran for 498 yards last year, 2nd in the league. Scrambles are slightly positive per play, so escaping is the one way he consistently beats the pressure.

strengths.title: McConkey connection works
strengths.body: When the ball goes to McConkey, the offense functions: +0.66 EPA per target and the best total of any of his targets. Tre Harris and Quentin Johnston are also positive. The receiver room isn't the problem, provided those players are healthy.

concerns.title: Sacks: line problem, and his habit
concerns.body: The Chargers allow the most quarterback hits in the league, and he is sacked on 10.4% of dropbacks, 40th of 45. His pressure-to-sack rate has risen almost every year of his career, so this is partly a trait. It isn't purely the line, which means better protection would help but wouldn't fix it.

concerns.title: Accuracy has fallen off
concerns.body: CPOE has swung 7.2 points from last year and his bad-throw rate is up 3.4 points. Throws to his right are the worst of it, at 10.3 points under expected. A career-long average-to-positive CPOE passer doesn't usually forget how to throw, so this should partly revert. Six games of it, though, is more than a blip.

concerns.title: Close-game collapse
concerns.body: Close fourth-quarter plays have produced -1.155 EPA per play, with 9 sacks in 28 snaps. That is where the 0-6 record has been decided. The sample is tiny and the per-play figure is extreme, so expect it to soften, but it reflects real pass-rush leverage when opponents know he must throw.

trend.note: Each of the last three games was worse than the one before by passing EPA, bottoming out at -14 in Kansas City. That stretch came against three top-five defenses, so schedule explains part of the drop.

nextGame.headline: Depleted Rams rush offers relief, but their deep shell doesn't
nextGame.body:
This Rams defense is good overall, 7th in EPA and 9th against the pass, but it doesn't get home. It ranks 30th in hit rate and 28th in sack rate. That is exactly the weakness that matches Herbert's biggest problem, and a clean pocket is the most direct path to a passable day. The catch is that Los Angeles allows almost nothing deep (2nd in deep EPA) or explosive (7th). It also smothers tight ends: top tight ends score 4.4 PPR under their averages against it, and Gadsden already struggles. Expect a dink-and-scramble game, with yardage coming from the WR2/WR3 spots where the Rams have been softer.

Availability tilts toward Herbert. The Rams' interior and edge rush is thinned: Kobie Turner and Poona Ford are on IR, and Myles Garrett's practice window may only open this coming week. Linebacker Nate Landman is out, and Trent McDuffie, a full-time corner, is listed out after missing last week. On the Chargers' side, left tackle Joe Alt and guard Kayode Awosika are questionable, and so are Tre Harris and McConkey. McConkey was in a no-contact jersey Monday. If Alt and McConkey both play coming off the bye, this is the best setup Herbert has had in weeks. If both sit, he faces an underdog script with his best target and best blocker gone.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers line vs a weak rush
keyMatchups.body: The offense that allows the most hits meets a defense that produces among the fewest. With Turner and Ford out, this is a rare week when Herbert's sack total should drop. Whether it holds depends on Alt's neck.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a lid
keyMatchups.body: The Rams are 2nd in deep EPA allowed, and Herbert is completing 30% of his 20+ yard throws with 3 interceptions. Forcing it downfield here is how a manageable game turns into another turnover day.

keyMatchups.title: Tight end looks are a dead end
keyMatchups.body: Gadsden has been his least efficient target by far, and the Rams are 3rd in EPA allowed to top tight ends. Volume should shift to the receivers, ideally McConkey if cleared.

nextGame.watch: His sack count. Against this rush he should stay under three; if he can't, the problem is more him than the line.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect improvement, not rescue. His interception rate (4.4%), his close-game EPA and his CPOE are all far outside a six-year track record and should drift back. The schedule just finished a run of three top-five defenses. What won't change quickly is the structure: a run-heavy offense that can't run, the worst protection in the league, and his own growing tendency to take sacks. That points to something like 185-225 passing yards a game with about a touchdown a game, interceptions easing toward one every game or so, and sacks staying high at roughly 2.5 to 3.8 a game. His rushing, around 22-38 yards a game, is the steadiest part of his line.

The upside case is a healthy Alt and McConkey together with the late-game disasters normalizing, which could put him back near league-average efficiency. The downside is that the offense stays 32nd, game scripts keep him passing from behind into known-pass downs, and the sack and turnover pace holds.
swingFactors: Joe Alt's health and the pass protection
Whether Harbaugh lets him throw earlier in downs

confidence.note: Six games that contradict a strong six-year career, with key blockers and receivers questionable.
